claims.text: History and exam usually suffice; some lesions need biopsy.
claims.quote: The history and physical examination are generally adequate for diagnosing many skin lesions. Some lesions require biopsy or further testing.

claims.text: Suspected melanoma: full-depth biopsy, excisional when feasible; biopsy even slightly suspect lesions.
claims.quote: Because early diagnosis can be lifesaving and features of melanoma can be variable, even slightly suspect lesions should be biopsied.

claims.text: Excisional biopsy for most lesions; broad shave biopsy on sensitive or cosmetically prominent sites. No radical surgery before histology.
claims.quote: Biopsy should be excisional for most lesions except those on anatomically sensitive or cosmetically prominent areas; in these cases, a broad shave biopsy can be performed.

claims.text: Suspected basal cell carcinoma: confirm with biopsy; histology sets the subtype and guides treatment.
claims.quote: The diagnosis of basal cell carcinoma consists of clinical evaluation of a suspicious skin lesion followed by confirmation with biopsy and histologic examination.

claims.text: Lipoma is clinical; biopsy or excise a rapidly growing one to exclude liposarcoma.
claims.quote: Diagnosis of lipomas is usually clinical, but a rapidly growing lesion should be biopsied or excised to exclude liposarcoma or other entities.
